findings.title: Picking Custom while Elite is shown snaps back to Elite for every real input (and seeds six fields anyway)
findings.area: Sensor Dial > Controls > Gestures preset (ui/pi-common.js:2917-2968, ui/pi-shell.js:209-215 and 242-244)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups (Elite) and dial-custom-gestures (Custom), Controls open, 373x410; task: switch Elite to Custom (the path the panel's help recommends) and Custom to Elite to Custom
findings.observed: MEASURED: with any trusted input (ArrowDown on the focused select, typeahead 'c', Alt+Down then ArrowDown+Enter in the popup, a real mouse press to open then keys) the stored controlPreset stays 'elite', the select shows Elite, the Custom rows stay hidden, and 6 gesture fields are written, each write carrying controlPreset 'elite'. A second attempt also fails (seeds already set, 0 writes, select snaps back). Custom to Elite to Custom ends on Elite (gestureTap 'pin' kept, 5 others seeded). Arrowing the closed select from Legacy passes Elite and ends on Elite. Only the detour Elite to Legacy to Custom reaches Custom (and skips the documented seeding). A synthetic dispatchEvent(new Event('change')) works (custom, 7 writes), which is what scripts/e2e-pi-panels.mjs:222-228 uses, so the suite stays green. READ cause: the seed runs from a document capture listener (2961-2968) and ends in hw.resyncBound() (2943); for a UA-dispatched event microtasks run between listeners, so the seed writes and the resync set the select back to the stored 'elite' before the shell's own element listener saves the pick, which then saves 'elite' (a no-op). READ history: v1.6.0 shipped the older sdpi-select seed without resyncBound; the capture listener came in b24ce39 (2026-09-24, untagged), so this is a 1.7-line regression present in 4bf09c0 and d03.
findings.evidence: p6-preset.json ('keyboard ArrowDown from elite': stored elite, shown elite, 6 writes all 'elite|6'); p6b log order: 'element input value=custom', six 'setSettings preset=elite', then 'doc-capture change value=elite', 'element change value=elite'; p6c-preset-confirm.json (typeahead, second attempt, popup, mouse+keys all elite; detour via Legacy reaches custom with 2 writes); p7-misc.json f (Custom->Elite->Custom ends elite).
findings.affected_user: everyone configuring dial gestures (mouse and keyboard alike)
findings.correction: Record the intent in the capture listener and run seedFromElite() only after the preset write has landed (setTimeout(0) after the dispatch, or from the controlPreset follower when it reads 'custom' with the intent set), or write controlPreset 'custom' first inside the same listener; resync only the six gesture selects, never the preset select. Add a suite check driven by trusted input (CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent typeahead or ArrowDown), not dispatchEvent.
findings.tradeoff: The Custom rows may paint the Legacy fallbacks for one frame before the seeded values appear; the seed must still never run on an echo or a replaced configuration document.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-groups at 373x410, Controls open, focus Gestures, send trusted 'c' (CDP key events): stored 'custom', select shows Custom, Custom rows visible, gestures equal the Elite map, every write after the first carries 'custom'. Repeat with ArrowDown and with Custom->Elite->Custom from dial-custom-gestures (gestureTap stays 'pin'). Real host: pick Custom on a real Elite dial, reselect the dial, it still shows Custom.

findings.title: Removing a rotation group lands focus on the next group's remove button; a double press or double click removes two groups, with no confirmation or undo
findings.area: Sensor Dial > Reading > Rotation groups (pi-common.js:3980-3995 removal; 565-589 focus memo by data-group index)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups plus Add group (3 groups: CPU:2, GPU:2, empty), 373x410; task: remove group 1 by keyboard and by mouse
findings.observed: MEASURED: Enter on group 1's x removes it and focus lands on the button now at group 1 (former group 2), with the same accessible name 'Remove group 1; its readings leave the rotation'. A second Enter removed the GPU group too; rotationKeys was written as []. A real mouse double click (two presses at the same point) on group 1's x (28x28 at x 347 of 373) also removed both populated groups, because the next group's x slides under the pointer. Merge sits 6 px from Add group and drops every group name in one click; Split afterwards gives one unnamed group holding everything plus an empty group 2.
findings.evidence: p3-groups.json G3 (before CPU:2, GPU:2, (unnamed):0; after two Enters only (unnamed):0; rotationKeysAfter []); p7-misc.json d (double click leaves only (unnamed):0, rotationKeys []), e (Add at x12 w79, Merge at x97, gap 6 px); p3 G4 (merge writes rotationGroups [], split gives names '', '').
findings.affected_user: keyboard and screen reader users (same name announced again), mouse users (double click), power users with curated groups
findings.correction: After a group removal, move focus to a non-destructive control (Add group, or the name field now at that index). For a group that holds readings, and for Merge when any group is named, reuse the panel's existing arm-then-confirm idiom from 'Replace shared settings': the first press arms and relabels ('Click again to remove group 1 and its 2 readings'), a second press within 5 s acts.
findings.tradeoff: One extra press for deliberate removals; the arm must reset on blur and timeout and be announced; tests that remove a group in one click need updating.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-groups plus Add group at 373x410: Enter, Enter on group 1's x removes exactly one group and focus is never on another group's x afterwards; a real double click on group 1's x removes at most one group; the other group's readings remain in rotationKeys; Merge with named groups needs a second press.

findings.title: Readings with the same label are indistinguishable in the rotation list and the detail tile editor
findings.area: Rotation list (pi-common.js rotationOption 410-448, syncRotationTools 508-524, startRotationRename 786-810); detail tiles (detailChip 1735-1854)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured with rotationKeys [Drive #0 'Drive Temperature', Drive #1 'Drive Temperature', CPU]; key-details (drive0 and drive1); 373x410; task: pick the right drive to reorder, rename or remove
findings.observed: MEASURED: both chips show 'Drive Temperature' with identical title, identical toolbar names ('Move Drive Temperature earlier', 'Remove Drive Temperature from the rotation') and the same rename label ('Name on the dial for Drive Temperature'); only the 'on dial' badge marks one. In the tile editor both remove buttons read 'Remove Drive Temperature from the detail list'. Only the checklist, under its source headers, tells them apart. READ: labels only, no duplicate handling anywhere.
findings.evidence: p3-groups.json G7, G7tools, G7rename, G7checklist; p4-details.json D4; p2-373.png and shot-key-details-press.png (two identical chips/tiles).
findings.affected_user: power users with identical hardware (multiple drives, GPUs, DIMMs); screen reader users cannot tell them apart at all
findings.correction: When two members of one list share a label, add the source: always in the title and in the accessible names (option, toolbar buttons, rename label, tile buttons), and a short visible suffix on the colliding chips only (for example 'Drive Temperature · #1' or the source's short name).
findings.tradeoff: Colliding chips get wider and may ellipsize at the 170 to 190 px chip cap; the source comes from the live tree, so a missing reading still shows its raw key.
findings.acceptance_test: The fixture above at 373x410: the two options' accessible names and titles differ and each names its source; the toolbar names differ when each is selected; key-details' two remove buttons have different accessible names.

findings.title: A long rotation is slow to reorder and the moving chip leaves the view
findings.area: Rotation list and its toolbar (pi-common.js moveSelectedRotation 752-760, selectRotationMember 544-562, placeRotationTools 527-540; pi.css .hw-set-tools 1408-1414)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured grown to all 37 sample readings; 373x410 (also 380x720 and 320x560); task: move the last member to first by mouse, then back by keyboard; remove and re-add one
findings.observed: MEASURED: the chip list is 480 px tall (15 rows) with the one toolbar below it (list top page y 458, toolbar 942). Last-to-first with Earlier: 36 clicks, 36 writes, the moved chip out of the viewport on 28 of 36 clicks (max chip-to-toolbar gap 422 px). By keyboard, Alt+Right 36 presses with the selected chip out of view on 17 (a move never scrolls it into view; a plain arrow selection does, line 556). No move-to-first/last. Removing member 5 and re-ticking it puts it at place 37 (32 moves to restore). 380x720: 2 of 36 clicks out of view; 320x560: 19 of 36.
findings.evidence: p2-373.json (geometry, mouseReorder, keyboardReorder, undoByRetick), p2-380.json, p2-320.json, p2-373.png.
findings.affected_user: power users with large rotations; keyboard; low vision
findings.correction: (a) After every move, scroll the moved chip into view with block 'nearest' (scroll-padding already clears the pinned header, pi.css:112). (b) Make the toolbar position: sticky; bottom: 0 with an opaque background while its list runs past the viewport. (c) Alt+Home and Alt+End move the selected member to the first or last place (keyboard only; toolbar keeps its four buttons).
findings.tradeoff: A sticky toolbar covers the bottom chip row (needs bottom scroll-padding) and must keep the grouped-mode slot guarantee that selecting moves nothing; auto-scroll can fight the user's own scroll; Alt+Home is a desktop Chrome shortcut (the app webview has no browser UI; Alt+PageUp/PageDown is the fallback); docs and sr-only help need the new keys.
findings.acceptance_test: Rerun p2 at 373x410: the moved chip is inside the viewport after every Earlier click and every Alt+Arrow press, the Earlier button never needs a scroll, and Alt+Home moves member 37 to place 1 with one keypress.

findings.title: The rotation checklist has no '+ all', so a multi-source set is built one tick and one scroll at a time
findings.area: Rotation checklist (pi-common.js 2755-2767, no onGroupAdd; factory support 2350-2362)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured, 373x410; task: add the other 34 sample readings to the rotation
findings.observed: MEASURED: the inline checklist is 158 px tall and shows 4 whole rows of 37; 34 ticks took 34 clicks, 30 in-list scrolls (1,054 px) and 4 page scrolls. The rotation checklist renders 0 '+ all' buttons; the detail checklist (same factory) renders 7 and added 21 readings in 3 presses with 3 writes.
findings.evidence: p2-373.json (checklist, build); p7-misc.json b (rotationChecklistAddAll 0, detailChecklistAddAll 7); p4-details.json D1 (clicks 4, writes 3).
findings.affected_user: power users building curated or grouped rotations
findings.correction: Give the rotation picker onGroupAdd: '+ all' adds the source's readings that are not yet members (alias-aware like setRotationMembership) to the collector group or the flat set, in tree order, as one write per field.
findings.tradeoff: Makes very large sets easy (overview and Reading colors grow with them); an empty set already means 'all of the picked sensor', so the gain is for multi-source sets and groups; must respect the runtime's first-group-wins dedupe.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-configured: open the checklist; the CPU header shows '+ all'; one press adds its 10 readings minus members, writes rotationKeys once (and rotationGroups once when grouped), ticks update in place and the list keeps its scroll.

findings.title: Moving a reading between rotation groups takes five actions and a search, and lands at the end
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups, 373x410; task: move CPU CCD1 from group 1 to group 2
findings.observed: MEASURED: select, Remove, set the collector radio to group 2, focus the search and type 'ccd1', tick: 5 clicks plus 4 typed characters and 4 writes; it lands last in group 2. 'Split into groups' puts every member in group 1 (collector on group 2), so sorting an existing set costs this per reading. Earlier at the first place and Later at the last place are disabled.
findings.evidence: p3-groups.json G2 (clicks 5, typedChars 4, writes 4, landedAt 2 of 3) and G4.
findings.correction: Let Earlier at the first place of group N move the member to the end of group N-1, and Later at the last place move it to the start of group N+1 (toolbar and Alt+Arrow), announced as 'moved to group X'; the flat set is unchanged.
findings.tradeoff: Repeated Earlier can overshoot into the previous group (visible, announced, undone by Later); a group emptied this way stays as an empty group, as today; the meaning of the list-end buttons changes.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-groups at 373x410: select CPU CCD1 (last in group 1), press Later: it is first in group 2, one write per field, selection and focus stay on it, and the announcement names group 2.

findings.title: Focus falls to the page after committing a group name (Enter or Tab) or a tile cell name (Enter)
findings.area: Rotation group name commit (pi-common.js 4053-4057, 4089-4097); detail cell rename (3940-3949)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups and key-details, 373x410; task: name a group, name several cells, by keyboard
findings.observed: MEASURED: Add group, type 'Drives', Enter: activeElement is BODY. Type a group 1 name, Tab: BODY, and the next Tab lands on group 1's collector radio (the start of the set, backwards), not the control after the name. Detail cell rename, Enter: BODY; the next Tab lands on tile 1's grip, so renaming a later cell means Tabbing back through every tile control. The rotation chip rename, by contrast, returns focus to its list.
findings.evidence: p3-groups.json G1 afterEnterFocus BODY; p7-misc.json c (focusAfterTab BODY, then 'New ticks go to group 1 (Processor)'); p4-details.json D3 (afterEnter BODY, nextTab 'Move tile 1'); p5-keyboard.json K3 focusEnd 'Rotation order'.
findings.affected_user: keyboard and screen reader users (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 focus order at risk when Tab sends focus backwards)
findings.correction: After the rebuild, restore focus: Enter on a group name returns to that name field (or its list); Tab lands on the element that follows the name in the new DOM (defer the rebuild one task and let the focus memo read the new activeElement); a cell rename's Enter returns to that cell's name button.
findings.tradeoff: A deferred rebuild must still never clobber typing in another field (guard at 676); with P02 unfixed, Tab from a group name lands on that group's remove button, so P02's arm should ship first.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-groups: type in group 2's name, Enter: focus on group 2's name field; type in group 1's name, Tab: focus on group 1's remove button (armed, nothing removed). key-details: rename cell 1, Enter: focus on that cell's name button; Tab: its down arrow.

findings.title: Group names and chip or cell renames are not saved when the pointer leaves the panel, unlike every bound text field
findings.area: pi-shell.js flush (115-130, bound fields only) vs rotation group name, chip rename and detail cell rename (commit on change only)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups, 373x410; task: type a group name or a chip rename, then leave the panel to select another key
findings.observed: MEASURED: typing a group name then dispatching mouseleave (the shell's flush trigger) writes 0 times; a synthetic window blur also writes 0; a chip rename typed then mouseleave writes 0; the bound Title field writes 1 on the same leave. INFERRED risk: pi-shell.js:124-130 records that the app tears a panel down when another action is selected and that pagehide saves never land (bench 20 of 20 lost). Whether QtWebEngine fires change on a focused field when the panel window deactivates is unknown here: headless Chrome kept document.hasFocus() true when another page came to the front (p10), so neither outcome could be reproduced.
findings.evidence: p3-groups.json G6 (groupNameWritesOnLeave 0, groupNameWritesOnWindowBlurEvent 0, renameWritesOnLeave 0, boundTitleWritesOnLeave 1); p10-blurchange.mjs output (hasFocusAfter true, no events).
findings.affected_user: power users naming groups and readings
findings.correction: Have the shell's flush (mouseleave and window blur) also commit a focused .hw-group-name, .hw-chip-rename or .hw-cell-rename by writing its value, without rebuilding the list under the caret.
findings.tradeoff: A half-typed name is saved when the pointer wanders out (the rule bound fields already follow); the commit must not re-render the editor mid-typing.
findings.acceptance_test: Real host (integrator): type a group name, click another key within 200 ms, reselect the dial: the name is stored, 20 of 20. Lab: type a group name, dispatch mouseleave: exactly one write carrying it, and the field keeps focus and caret.

findings.title: New ticks go back to group 1 on every fresh page
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups, 373x410; task: keep filling group 2 after switching keys away and back

findings.title: Keyboard accelerators are invisible inside the panel
findings.area: Rotation lists (F2, Delete, Alt+Arrow), section titles (Alt-click), tile grips (arrows)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured and key-configured, 373x410; task: a sighted keyboard user discovering faster edits
findings.observed: MEASURED: no visible help mentions F2, Delete or Alt with an arrow (they are in sr-only #rotation-keys-help and in docs/sensor-dial.md:40 and 114); Alt-click on a section title appears only in the fold buttons' tooltip; 0 elements carry aria-keyshortcuts.
findings.correction: Add aria-keyshortcuts to the rotation lists ('Alt+ArrowLeft Alt+ArrowRight F2 Delete') and the shortcut to each toolbar button's title ('Earlier (Alt+Left)').
findings.tradeoff: Tooltip text only; nothing visible is added; titles must stay in step with the handlers.
findings.acceptance_test: Each rotation toolbar button's title names its shortcut; both list kinds expose aria-keyshortcuts; axe still reports 0 violations at 373 and 320 wide.

keep_unchanged: Rotation keyboard model: one Tab stop per list, one roving toolbar, F2/Delete/Alt+Arrow as shortcuts for visible buttons; a chip rename's Enter returns focus to its list. Adding two readings, moving one and renaming it from a fresh page took 22 keystrokes and 4 writes (MEASURED p5 K3).

Fold memory per panel kind across fresh pages: Alerts opened on one dial is open on the next (p5 K1b); Fold all plus opening Alerts puts Warn at viewport y 366 on the next dial's first screen, 7 Tabs from the top (p7 a). Folding writes nothing.

Detail list arrow chains: Enter on the up arrow moved a reading 24 places with focus following it and the chip in view on all 24 presses (p4 D2); '+ all' in the detail checklist added 21 readings in 3 presses and 3 writes.
Four-reading keys: Reading 4 is 13 Tabs from the top and changing it took 23 keystrokes and 1 write (p5 K4); switching quad to single to quad keeps every slot, label and color (p7 g).
Scale: with a 2,000-reading tree the filter costs at most 2.4 ms per keystroke, a tick 2.1 ms median (4.5 max) and a rotation move 4.6 ms median with 60 members (p8).
The rotation checklist keeps its typed filter and stays open while ticking; tick states sync in place without losing the list's scroll (p2, p5 K3).
Legacy to Custom by mouse: one write, no seeding; 'What the dial does now' lists only the gestures other settings change under Custom (p6).
Theme strip: named chips, one Tab stop, arrows browse and pick (READ pi-common.js 3621-3632).
Primary picker: Enter commits the top match only for a typed filter (READ 2602-2611).
own_regression_risks: P01: running the seed a task later can race an echo or a replaced document; the seed must stay tied to the person's pick, and the new suite check must use trusted input or it will pass for the wrong reason again.
P02: arm-then-confirm adds a press and a timer; the relabel must be announced and reset on blur; the new focus target must survive the rebuild.

P04: a sticky toolbar can cover the bottom chip row and must not move under the pointer in grouped mode (slot guarantee); auto-scroll after moves can fight the user's own scroll; Alt+Home is a desktop Chrome shortcut (use Alt+PageUp/PageDown if the webview reserves it).
P05: '+ all' can create very large sets in one press, growing the overview and the Reading colors list with them.
P06: cross-group moves change what Earlier and Later mean at list ends; an overshoot moves a reading into another group (visible and announced).

P07: deferring the rebuild after a name commit must not break the 'never rebuild under a focused name field' guard (pi-common.js:676); Tab from a group name lands on its remove button, so P02 must ship first.
P08: committing names on pointer leave saves half-typed names and must not re-render the editor under the caret.
P09: moving the density row changes the Press section's reading order, docs images, alt text and any order assumptions in the suites.
P10: a derived collector can surprise users who expect group 1.
P03: a visible source suffix widens colliding chips and can ellipsize at the chip cap.
not_run: The real Stream Deck app and QtWebEngine: P01's real select popup and P08's window-deactivation change semantics need the integrator's real-host check (headless Chrome could not model window deactivation: document.hasFocus() stayed true).
The app's DevTools port, the installed plugin, HWiNFO (by rule).
NVDA and Narrator, Windows High Contrast, OS text scaling, touch, a real hand-driven drag and drop.
